Subject: Operational plan: version-pinning matrix and emergency rollback lattice

Hi team,

We need to lock down the private/VPC upgrade approach for Acme before the August maintenance window. Attached is a working pinning matrix (pinning-matrix-v3.xlsx) and an early rollback playbook. Goal: a concise set of rules we can hand to Acme's ops and our on-call so upgrades are predictable and revertible.

High-level ask: please review and respond with concrete changes by EOD Monday so we can publish the final plan and DocuSign the maintenance SLA. Key items to confirm:
- Version pinning policy: semantic pin by major.minor (e.g., 2.3.x) vs strict build pinning for runtime-critical components.
- Maintenance window: proposed weekly risk window on Saturdays 02:00–06:00 UTC (Acme prefers at least 4 hours).
- Rollback lattice: define multi-stage rollback (canary -> partial -> full) and the abort thresholds.
- Network considerations: planned BGP or route updates, NAT gateway drain, and firewall rule push ordering.
- Validation gating: smoke tests, perf targets, and KV cache consistency checks.

Quick summary of proposed pinning matrix (details in attachment):
1) Control plane services: strict build pin (no minor auto-updates).
2) Worker runtime: allow minor auto-updates with canary first (2% traffic), then 10%, then 100%.
3) Model artifacts: content-addressable pins + manifest signature verification.

Immediate questions for Acme (Maria): any blackout periods in July/August we should avoid? Also, confirm whether your procurement team requires a separate change notice (procure-team@acme-corp.com is cc'd).

Attachments: pinning-matrix-v3.xlsx, rollback-playbook-v1.pdf, network-diagram.png

Thanks,
Priyom

+1 on the matrix — a couple of practical notes from preflight/QA:
- For worker runtime, require a preflight checksum+smoke-run against a staging snapshot (not live traffic) before the 2% canary.
- Add an explicit KV-cache-drain step before switching the routing for the canary nodes; without it we've seen cache-coherence stalls.
- For control plane pinning, add an exception flow for security-hotfixes: these must still go through a fast-track review and include a fallback build id.

On the maintenance window, Acme's production teams prefer Saturday 02:00–05:00 UTC (3 hours). We should build the plan for a 4-hour window but show an optional compressed 3-hour runbook (fast path) if Acme approves.

Suggested owners (I can take staging validation and smoke-run checklist):
- Staging validation & smoke: Monica Patel
- Network change orchestration: Soojin Lee
- Rollback coordination & docs: Priyom Das
- On-call escalation: Dev Patel

Thanks — a few operational constraints from networking I want to call out before we lock the schedule:

1) BGP baseline: if we're doing any BGP adj changes for private cross-connects, those must be done in the first 30 minutes of the window and monitored for route convergence. If convergence >120s we trigger canary abort.

2) NAT gateway drains: plan to rotate NATs one AZ at a time; metric to gate is <0.5% packet drops and completion of TCP drain within 90s.

3) Firewall rule push ordering: push ingress deny rules after egress flows are stable to avoid accidental lockouts for health checks.

4) Canary topology: proposed canary cluster should be isolated by route-tag and have its own telemetry stream. We should not let canary traffic hit the global KV cache — use a read-through cache seeded from snapshot instead.

Operational gating metrics (suggested):
- Error rate (5m) < 0.5%
- 99th latency < baseline + 200ms
- Token generation throughput within 10% of baseline for sustained 10m

If any gate trips, we move to rollback-lattice stage 1 (fail-fast revert to previous artifact, warm-up traffic split to 0%). Stage 2 is partial revert of routing; stage 3 is full revert + network rollback. Details in rollback-playbook-v1.pdf.

Priyom / team,

Thanks for the summary and the attachments. A couple of constraints from Acme side:
- Blackout windows: no changes during monthly billing close (first 72 hours of each month). For August, our preferred maintenance window is Saturday 02:00–05:00 UTC.
- SLA for rollback: we require documented RTO <= 90 minutes for full revert to the previous release and confirmation of data integrity (KV + model manifests).
- We will supply a change approval contact and a secondary on-call mobile for the maintenance date.

We do not block the proposed plan but want the RTO/RPO and canary gating metrics added to the DocuSign change form. Also, our procurement team will route a formal change notice — I'll loop them in after we finalize the schedule.

Subject: Re: Operational plan: version-pinning matrix and emergency rollback lattice — final decisions and next steps

Team — thanks for the rapid replies. Summary of decisions and assignments (finalizing for DocuSign):

1) Pinning policy
  - Control plane: strict build pin. Security hotfix fast-track allowed with approval chain documented in the playbook.
  - Worker runtime: semantic minor pinning (major.minor.x); auto-rolls limited to canary sequence (2% -> 10% -> 100%).
  - Models: immutable manifest pins + signature verification.

2) Maintenance window
  - Agreed: Saturday 02:00–05:00 UTC (3-hour primary window). We will include an optional 4-hour contingency in the runbook.

3) Rollback lattice
  - Stage 1: Fail-fast revert artifact, traffic split to previous cluster (0% to candidate).
  - Stage 2: Partial network routing revert (per-AZ) if metrics remain bad after 10 minutes.
  - Stage 3: Full revert + NAT/BGP rollback and post-mortem.
  - RTO target: <= 90 minutes (Acme requirement). RPO: model manifest integrity guaranteed; KV restore path documented.

4) Owners
  - Staging validation & smoke: Monica Patel (action: finalize checklist by Tue 07/24).
  - Network orchestration & BGP tests: Soojin Lee (action: coordinate CloudOps sim by Mon 07/23).
  - Rollback coordination & DocuSign: Priyom Das (action: publish final playbook and DocuSign link by Tue 07/24).
  - On-call escalation & incident comms: Dev Patel.

5) Docs and approvals
  - I've attached a consolidated rollback-playbook-v1.pdf and updated pinning matrix; final DocuSign link: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/file/id12345-pinning-matrix.
  - Maria: will you confirm the change-approval contact so we can embed it in the DocuSign form?

6) Preflight checklist (to execute in the hour before the window)
  - Snapshot KV and upload manifest to immutable storage.
  - Run staging smoke-run and perf baseline.
  - Ensure telemetry streams for canary cluster are active.
  - Confirm legal/procurement change notice queued.

If no objections, I'll send the DocuSign packet to Acme and schedule the dry-run with CloudOps next week.

Thanks — Priyom
